events.text: A crane lands on your sill with a slip from {npc}, the characters smudged. The academy's isle drifts too far from home, {he} writes, and the other children were born above the clouds and laugh at how {he} holds a brush.

effects.log: Your reply goes down the cloud road with a crane. It says you are proud, and you mean it.

events.text: The academy's discipline hall sends {npc} home on a cloud with a slip of jade sealed at both ends: expelled, for a fight in the courtyard that broke a pillar older than the academy. {npc} steps off the cloud and does not look up.

choices.text: Take {npc} in, and say nothing about the pillar

effects.log: {npc} carries {his} bag to {his} room and cries only once the door is shut.

mem.note: did not shout when I was sent home

choices.text: Go to the discipline hall and plead

effects.log: You stand before the hall and answer for the pillar yourself. They keep {npc}, on the last warning there is.

mem.note: went before the hall for me

choices.text: Tell {npc} the truth: this was earned

effects.log: You say it plainly. {npc} looks at the floor for a long while and then nods.

mem.note: told me I deserved it

events.text: A master of the academy comes to your isle in person, which is a great courtesy above the clouds, and asks to take {npc} as a direct disciple: {his} own breath, {his} own rules, and nothing kept back.

effects.log: The master bows to you as an equal. {npc} kneels to the master. Both of them look as if the clouds might drop them.

mem.note: let me become a direct disciple

effects.log: The master leaves without argument. {npc} does not speak to you for a month.

mem.note: refused the master for me

events.text: {npc} comes home from the academy for good, sixteen now, with a sealed slip of jade from the masters and a way of standing on the clouds that you do not remember teaching.

effects.log: You read it twice. Then you look at {npc} for a long time.
You cook. {npc} eats like a storm hawk. The slip waits on the table until the bowls are empty.

mem.note: fed me before asking anything

events.text: Your kingdom of the Isles is a month old, and the first quarrel of the court is already on your table: the cloud-farmers want a bridge between the two largest isles, and the guard want new spears before anything else.

effects.log: The bridge is strung by the next gathering. The farmers remember who strung it.
The guard cheer you at the muster. The farmers wait, and notice.

choices.text: Let an archivist write the laws first

effects.log: The laws are long and fair and nobody reads them. They hold anyway.

events.text: An envoy of the Jade Court comes to your kingdom with a scroll: the Court would like to hear you kneel, once, at the next gathering, and the matter of your crown will be considered settled.

effects.log: You kneel. The Court is satisfied. Your own people watch it from the back of the hall.

choices.text: Send the envoy home with a gift and no answer

effects.log: The envoy goes. The answer that is not an answer gets to the Court ahead of the envoy.
Your court cheers. Somewhere across the clouds an order begins counting its wings.

events.text: A drifting fleet of war-isles has anchored off your kingdom's edge, flying the banner of a house that thinks your isles were theirs before the clouds moved.

ok.log: You hold the edge for three days. On the fourth the fleet weighs anchor and drifts away a little smaller.

fail.log: The edge breaks. You are carried back to your hall, and two small isles go with the fleet when it leaves.

choices.text: Hold the walls and let the wind decide

effects.log: The fleet waits a season for a wind that does not come, and goes home.
The fleet sails away paid. Your kingdom is the same size, and lighter.

events.text: A blight has gone through the cloud-orchards of half your isles. The farmers come to the hall carrying the black fruit in their hands, and they do not shout. That is worse.

effects.log: Nobody goes hungry. The farmers carry the story of it to every isle that will listen.

choices.text: Keep the stores for the guard

effects.log: The guard eat. The orchards do not forget.

events.text: Your court of the Isles has split down the middle: the wing-captains want the kingdom to grow by force, the archivists want it to grow by treaty, and both have brought lists of the other side's mistakes.

effects.log: Three archivists go home to their own isles. The treaties go with them.
The captains grumble on the walls. The ledgers balance for the first time.
Both halves of your court are furious with you, which up here passes for peace.
